note: The first 4 attacker-controlled bytes are reinterpreted as parser flags and influence parser behavior.
The next 4 attacker-controlled bytes become renderer flags and are passed into the HTML renderer.

code: md_html(data, size, process_output, out, parser_flags, renderer_flags);
note: The remaining bytes are treated as Markdown input and handed to the vulnerable Markdown-to-HTML pipeline.

code: MD_PARSER parser = { ... parser_flags, enter_block_callback, leave_block_callback, enter_span_callback, leave_span_callback, text_callback, debug_log_callback, NULL };
note: The attacker-controlled parser flags are copied into the parser configuration that drives parsing and rendering callbacks.
During parsing, MD4C builds internal text buffers from the attacker-controlled Markdown stream and propagates substrings into attribute builders.
Raw attribute text is copied byte-by-byte into a temporary attribute buffer, preserving attacker-controlled characters such as entity delimiters and punctuation.
The parser records substring boundaries for the attribute, creating a sequence of spans that the renderer later iterates over.
The renderer walks the attacker-influenced substring table to emit each piece of the attribute value.
Each substring length is derived from adjacent offsets; malformed or extreme span layouts can drive incorrect size calculations.

code: for(i = 3; i < size-1; i++) codepoint = 16 * codepoint + hex_val(text[i]);
note: When a substring is parsed as a numeric entity, attacker-controlled digits are accumulated into a codepoint value.
The computed codepoint is converted to UTF-8 bytes and appended to the output buffer through the callback.
The harness discards output, so the crash must occur inside parsing/rendering before the callback returns.
